source: NMC MD Pharmacology 2022 curriculum; PGMER 2023; unsourced (owner-approved) teaching-methodology items; web refs from earlier pass

cards.front: What does the NMC teaching-skills assessment in the MD Pharmacology practical exam include?
cards.back: Assessment of teaching or presentation skills, for example presenting an undergraduate lecture, making a question paper, or writing learning objectives; and a discussion on the dissertation.
refs: NMC MD Pharmacology 2022 curriculum (practical exam, component d)

cards.front: What does SMART stand for in a learning objective?
cards.back: Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant and Time-bound. A SMART objective states exactly what the learner will be able to do, how it will be judged, and by when.
refs: UNSOURCED - owner must verify

cards.front: What are the ABCD parts of a well-written learning objective?
cards.back: Audience (who will learn), Behaviour (the observable action, as an action verb), Condition (under what circumstances or with what resources) and Degree (the standard to be reached).
refs: UNSOURCED - owner must verify

cards.front: What are the three domains of learning that the NMC groups MD Pharmacology competencies under?
cards.back: Cognitive (knowledge and thinking), affective (attitudes, professionalism, communication) and psychomotor (practical skills). Each competency is predominantly in one domain. The practical exam focuses mainly on psychomotor; the viva on psychomotor and affective.
refs: NMC MD Pharmacology 2022 curriculum (subject-specific competencies A, B, C; practical and viva)

cards.front: Classify: levels of the cognitive domain in revised Bloom's taxonomy (lowest to highest)
refs: UNSOURCED - owner must verify

cards.front: Why should "know" and "understand" be avoided in objectives? Give better verbs.
cards.back: They cannot be observed or measured. Use action verbs that match the level: list or define (recall), explain or classify (understanding), calculate or prescribe (application), compare or interpret (analysis), justify or appraise (evaluation), demonstrate or perform (skills).
refs: UNSOURCED - owner must verify

cards.front: Write a SMART objective for a class on loading dose.
cards.back: Example: "At the end of this 45-minute session, each second-year MBBS student will be able to calculate the loading dose of a drug from its target plasma concentration, volume of distribution and bioavailability, correctly in at least four of five given problems."
refs: KDT8 ch3
UNSOURCED - owner must verify

cards.front: Short note: Components of a lesson plan

points: Topic, target learners and their prior knowledge, date, duration, venue
Specific learning objectives across the domains needed
Set induction (opening)
Content in logical steps, each with method and teaching aid
Learner activity and questions
Summary and closure
How achievement of each objective will be checked
Resources and references; assignment or follow-up

refs: UNSOURCED - owner must verify
WEB Indian J Pharmacol Microteaching: overview and examination evaluation 2023 https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10657622/

cards.front: What is set induction in a lesson?
cards.back: The opening of a lesson that gains attention and rapport, using examples or devices and linking to what learners already know.
refs: WEB Indian J Pharmacol Microteaching: overview and examination evaluation 2023 https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10657622/

cards.front: What is micro-teaching and what is its cycle?
cards.back: A scaled-down lesson: a short session for a small group that practises one teaching skill at a time. Cycle: plan, teach, observe with supervisor feedback, re-plan, re-teach, re-observe.
refs: WEB Indian J Pharmacol Microteaching: overview and examination evaluation 2023 https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10657622/

cards.front: Which teaching skills are practised in micro-teaching?
cards.back: Lesson planning; set induction; presentation and explanation; stimulus variation; audiovisual aids; reinforcement; probing questions; classroom management; closure.
refs: WEB Indian J Pharmacol Microteaching: overview and examination evaluation 2023 https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10657622/

cards.front: Essay: Delivering a short undergraduate lecture in the practical exam (step-wise)

points: Choose a focused topic and write 2-3 SMART objectives
Make a lesson plan with timing; pick suitable aids
Introduce yourself and the topic; state the objectives
Set induction: a case or question linked to practice
Move from simple to complex in a logical order
Use examples, a diagram or flow chart; check understanding with questions
Keep eye contact, clear voice and steady pace; avoid reading slides
Summarise key points against the objectives
Ask a few assessment questions; invite questions
Keep to the time given; accept examiner feedback

refs: UNSOURCED - owner must verify
WEB Indian J Pharmacol Microteaching: overview and examination evaluation 2023 https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10657622/

cards.front: Which teaching-learning methods does the NMC PG guideline expect a pharmacology PG to apply?
cards.back: Classroom lectures, self-directed learning, case-based learning, case discussions, integrated teaching, small group discussions, seminars, journal clubs and research presentations; also computer-assisted learning.
refs: NMC MD Pharmacology 2022 curriculum (competency A, Teaching and Assessment 3; teaching-learning methods)

cards.front: What is DOAP?
cards.back: Demonstrate, Observe, Assist, Perform: the NMC names it as a method for laboratory and bedside sessions, alongside skill-lab simulations and case-based discussions.
refs: NMC MD Pharmacology 2022 curriculum (teaching-learning methods E)

cards.front: How often should journal clubs and seminars run in MD Pharmacology, and how are they assessed (NMC)?
cards.back: Journal club and student seminar: at least once every 1-2 weeks; symposium at least once in 3 months. Journal club presents and critically appraises original research; the presenter is graded by faculty and the grade recorded in the logbook. Seminars are graded by faculty and peers.
refs: NMC MD Pharmacology 2022 curriculum (teaching-learning methods B, C, D)

cards.front: Lecture versus small-group teaching: what does the NMC say?
cards.back: Didactic lectures should be used sparingly; the NMC suggests a minimum of 10 lectures a year in a PG department. It recommends a judicious mix of methods, including small group discussions, seminars, journal clubs and case-based learning.
refs: NMC MD Pharmacology curriculum PDF p14

cards.front: How do you choose an audiovisual aid for a lesson?
cards.back: Match it to the objective, group size, room and time: chalkboard or whiteboard for building a diagram step by step; flip chart for small groups; slides for images, graphs and large groups; video or simulation for processes and experiments; models and real dosage forms for identification. The aid should support, not replace, the teacher.
refs: UNSOURCED - owner must verify

cards.front: Short note: Making effective slides

points: One idea per slide, a short headline
Few lines and few words per line; key words, not paragraphs
Large readable font, strong contrast, simple consistent background
Diagrams and graphs rather than tables of numbers
Do not read the slides aloud; face the audience
Allow time per slide; end with a summary slide

refs: UNSOURCED - owner must verify
WEB Indian J Pharmacol Microteaching: overview and examination evaluation 2023 https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10657622/

cards.front: What is the place of computer-assisted learning (CAL) in teaching pharmacology?
cards.back: The NMC expects PGs to know the utility of computer-assisted learning and use it to promote learning of pharmacology. Amphibian, dog and cat experiments should be done with computer-assisted simulation models or facilities. Alternatives to animal use follow the 3Rs (replacement, reduction, refinement).
refs: NMC MD Pharmacology 2022 curriculum (competency A, Teaching and Assessment 5; animal experiments note)
Sarkar p281-285

cards.front: Formative versus summative assessment.
cards.back: Formative: during training, to give feedback and improve learning (in MD Pharmacology, internal assessment covering all domains, with quarterly review). Summative: at the end, to certify competence (the final theory, practical and viva).
refs: NMC MD Pharmacology 2022 curriculum (assessment: formative and summative)
PGMER 2023 s8.1

cards.front: What qualities make an assessment good?
cards.back: Validity (measures what it is meant to measure), reliability (consistent results), objectivity (uniform marking) and practicability (feasible within time and resources).
refs: WEB Indian J Pharmacol Standardization and validation of OSPE in pharmacology 2017 https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5754933/

cards.front: Short note: Setting a question paper

points: Table mapping topics against domains or levels, with marks for each, based on the objectives and their importance
Long essay, short notes and objective items in set proportions
Cover recall, application and problem solving
Clear and unambiguous, with action verbs and marks shown
Avoid "write all you know"
Model answer and marking scheme prepared in advance
Review by a colleague before use

refs: WEB Indian J Pharmacol Standardization and validation of OSPE in pharmacology 2017 https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5754933/ (blueprint part only)
NMC MD Pharmacology curriculum PDF p22

cards.front: Parts of a single-best-answer MCQ, and common writing faults.
cards.back: Stem (case or question), lead-in, the key (correct answer) and distractors (plausible wrong options). Faults: clues in grammar or length, "all of the above" or "none of the above", negative stems, implausible distractors, and testing trivia.
refs: UNSOURCED - owner must verify

cards.front: How can essay questions be made more objective?
cards.back: Use structured or modified essay questions with defined parts and marks, a clear task, and a model answer with a key; use more short-answer questions to sample more content; mark question by question rather than paper by paper.
refs: WEB Cureus Structured and conventional viva voce in pharmacology teaching 2026 https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13279708/ (predefined scoring and standard questions part only)
UNSOURCED - owner must verify

cards.front: What makes feedback effective?
cards.back: Timely and frequent (the NMC stresses this so students can improve); specific; based on observed behaviour, not personality; descriptive rather than judgemental; balanced between strengths and areas to improve; limited to a few points; and ending with an action plan.
refs: NMC MD Pharmacology 2022 curriculum (formative assessment: important instructions)
WEB Br J Clin Pharmacol Formative feedback to improve pharmacology learning: proposed principles 2026 https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13421061/
UNSOURCED - owner must verify

cards.front: Describe Pendleton's rules for giving feedback.
cards.back: The learner first says what went well; the observer then says what went well; the learner says what could be improved; the observer then says what could be improved. The method is learner-led and encourages self-reflection.
refs: WEB BMC Med Educ Feedback in the clinical setting 2020 https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7712594/

cards.front: What is the "sandwich" method of feedback, and its drawback?
cards.back: A point to improve sits between two positive comments. It is weakened because learners expect the criticism and discount the constructive content.
refs: WEB Cureus Development and evaluation of the Joseph-RATA structured feedback model in undergraduate pharmacology 2026 https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13589777/

cards.front: Which criteria are used to mark a teaching presentation (microteaching)?
cards.back: Content; demonstration; clarity of presentation and explanation; interaction with learners; time management and pacing; questioning; and closure.
refs: WEB Indian J Pharmacol Microteaching: overview and examination evaluation 2023 https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10657622/

cards.front: How often must teaching skills be assessed during MD Pharmacology training (NMC)?
cards.back: At least two sessions dedicated to assessing teaching skills every year; good teaching practice is assessed in every academic activity the PG conducts. The log book, signed by the head of department, is produced in original at the final practical exam.
refs: NMC MD Pharmacology 2022 curriculum (teaching-learning methods I and J: teaching skills, log book)

cards.front: What is the main weakness of a traditional viva, and what does a structured viva add?
cards.back: A traditional viva is criticised for subjectivity, low reliability, inter-examiner variability and bias. A structured viva uses standard questions, a predefined scoring scheme and uniform administration, improving objectivity and reliability.
refs: WEB Cureus Structured and conventional viva voce in pharmacology teaching 2026 https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13279708/

cards.front: Which unit trains MD Pharmacology PG students in education methods and assessment techniques (NMC)?
cards.back: The Medical Education Unit (MEU) or Department of Medical Education (DOME).
refs: NMC MD Pharmacology 2022 curriculum (teaching-learning methods I)

cards.front: What teaching role do PG students take on, and who gives feedback on it (NMC)?
cards.back: They conduct undergraduate classes in various courses; a faculty member observes the session and gives feedback on the PG teaching skills.
refs: NMC MD Pharmacology 2022 curriculum (teaching-learning methods I)

cards.front: Which two curricula must an MD Pharmacology PG be aware of for teaching (NMC)?
cards.back: The salient features of the undergraduate medical curriculum in India, and the postgraduate medical education curriculum and guidelines in India.
refs: NMC MD Pharmacology 2022 curriculum (competency A, Teaching and Assessment 1 and 2)

cards.front: What teaching skill does PGMER 2023 list among PG training goals?
cards.back: Basic skills in teaching medical and paramedical professionals; PGs should become competent specialists and medical teachers.
refs: PGMER 2023 s1.1 (focus and goal, v)

cards.front: Who conducts formative and summative assessment in PG medical exams, and what does each include?
cards.back: The medical college conducts formative assessment and the university conducts summative assessment; both have theory, clinical or practical and viva voce components.
refs: PGMER 2023 s8.1

cards.front: Which theory paper of the MD Pharmacology summative exam covers education?
cards.back: Paper III: clinical pharmacology, experimentation, research, biostatistics and education.
refs: NMC MD Pharmacology 2022 curriculum (summative examination, theory papers)

cards.front: What must MD Pharmacology internal assessment cover, and how often?
cards.back: Theory and practical or clinical exams, held frequently, covering all domains of learning, professionalism and communication skills, with feedback to improve learning; quarterly assessment is included.
refs: NMC MD Pharmacology 2022 curriculum (formative assessment, quarterly)

cards.front: Which domains should the viva voce test in the MD Pharmacology summative exam?
cards.back: Psychomotor and affective domains, testing overall knowledge of the subject. Each examiner conducts the viva separately.
refs: NMC MD Pharmacology 2022 curriculum (summative examination, part 3)

cards.front: How many examiners assess an MD Pharmacology thesis, and when must it be submitted?
cards.back: At least three: one internal and two external, none of whom examine the theory or clinical exams. The thesis is submitted at least six months before the theory and clinical or practical examinations.
refs: NMC MD Pharmacology 2022 curriculum (summative examination, part 1: thesis)

cards.front: How much of the MD practical and viva marks is given for the dissertation?
cards.back: 5% of the practical or clinical and viva total (20 of 400 marks), counted within the practical marks. An external examiner from outside the state assesses the dissertation and its viva.
refs: PGMER 2023 M.D. criteria for evaluation (dissertation 5%)

cards.front: What forms may the PG theory examination take?
cards.back: Descriptive (long or short answer) questions, multiple-choice questions, or a mix of both.
refs: PGMER 2023 s8.3 A(a)

cards.front: What presentation skills must an MD Pharmacology PG demonstrate (NMC)?
cards.back: Presentation skills in a classroom setting and at academic meetings at local and national levels.
refs: NMC MD Pharmacology 2022 curriculum (psychomotor competencies, mandatory 6)

cards.front: What does the NMC list among psychomotor skills for teaching and assessment material?
cards.back: Demonstrating skills to prepare material for teaching-learning and assessment.
refs: NMC MD Pharmacology 2022 curriculum (psychomotor competencies, mandatory 9)
